clue.text: Scowl about rating work

indicators.note: the scowl word is placed around the rating, enclosing it

parts.note: to lour (or lower) is to frown or scowl
an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

explanation.surface: Someone frowns at the grade their work has been given.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is toil or effort, a straightforward synonym for work as a noun.

clue.text: Repeatedly curtailed fashionable mission

indicators.note: the tail is cut off twice over, so the phrase loses its last letter and then its new last letter

parts.note: à la mode means in fashion

explanation.surface: A trendy mission keeps having its funding cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo in Texas began as a Spanish mission before becoming the famous fort of 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was originally a Spanish Catholic mission, so it is an example of a mission building.

clue.text: Roofless old enclosure corporation cocked up

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the word means reading it from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a large belly, as is pot

explanation.surface: An old pen built by a company has been botched and left without a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocked up' reads as British slang for bungled, but here it means turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-top vehicle has no roof, so the hyphenated adjective means roofless.

clue.text: Unexpectedly uncordial portent of downfall

parts.note: the word is taken as written and its nine letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone's sudden rudeness is a sign that they are heading for a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' reads as ruin but means rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark cloud heralds a fall of rain, so it portends a downpour.

clue.text: Cutting small investigation

parts.note: a hearing is an inquiry, as before a tribunal

explanation.surface: A minor inquiry into budget cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearing is cutting, as of wool from sheep or metal with shears.

clue.text: Team, aquiver, checking grass in a hysterical manner

parts.note: a side is a team
tingly means quivering with excitement
to grass, or split, is British slang for informing on someone

clue.text: Source of down clue I derided to some extent

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of clue, the I, and the start of derided

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like crossword jargon but means soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider duck is the bird whose soft breast feathers give eiderdown.

clue.text: Terse, exhausted Dee perhaps embraces Rosie, for one?

explanation.definitionFit: Rosie the Riveter is the WWII American poster figure of a female factory worker.

clue.text: Nobody else thereon — on manoeuvres

taken as written, the second part of the fodder

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'none other' means no other person, used for emphasis.

clue.text: Finally, sound barrier broken — it's unique

indicators.note: the letters are smashed and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, it joins the anagram fodder

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is taken

clue.text: The majority of men on speaking terms to begin with

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words spell the answer

clue.text: Actors helping removal in theatre?

a ration is a portion or helping of food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests the stage, but it is an operating theatre.

clue.text: Scoring which you'd paradoxically relinquish aim

a goal is an aim

explanation.surface: A paradox: to score you must let go of what you are aiming at.
explanation.walkthrough: A drop goal is a rugby score made by drop-kicking the ball over the bar; the paradox is that it reads as giving up your goal.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a drop goal is a method of scoring three points, so it names a kind of score.

clue.text: Beaming about mostly stuffed bloke

clue.text: Origin of some Kurdish tribal revolutionary

only a portion of the phrase is used

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of Kurdish and the start of tribal

clue.text: Recklessly go in centre of Turkish bath, scorching

parts.note: its central letter, the fourth of seven, is used
taken as written, the rest of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Plunging recklessly into the heart of a sweltering Turkish bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Baking-hot means extremely hot, as hot as an oven, so scorching.

clue.text: Skilfully handle participants

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to deal deftly with
second meaning: all those taking part in a race or contest

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone managing a group, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for dealing with something deftly and as a noun for all the competitors in an event.

clue.text: Pornography books Heather hides

the OT, Old Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a name but is the plant.

clue.text: Farewell from curt janitor that's parted and rejoined anew?

cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a caretaker looks after a building

clue.text: Moose, caught up in estate, maybe one crying raucously

clue.text: Share everything, rotating most important Mexican food

clue.text: Lead fitting hides early sign of dry rot

having a fit, so the letters are thrown about

indicators.note: only the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead fitting' reads as a plumbing part but is the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to go bad, as an egg rots; addled eggs are rotten.

clue.text: Ape takes cover, dropping article

an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An ape shelters but sheds a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like the animal but is the verb to imitate.

clue.text: Bug peerage on vacation with First Lady

explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests the US President's wife, but it means Eve.

clue.text: Accepting greeting, strip buttocks

hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A stripper waves hello and bares their bottom.

explanation.definitionFit: Behind is an informal word for a person's bottom or rump.

clue.text: Right accounts missing introduction

parts.note: stories are accounts or narratives

explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of the British Conservative Party, the political right.
